Council approves transit plan after heated debate

By A. Reporter · November 8, 2026

The city council voted 7 to 2 on Tuesday to approve a $40 million plan to extend bus service to the northern suburbs, ending months of bitter argument over the city's budget.

Critics slammed the scheme as a reckless giveaway to well-connected developers, while supporters hailed it as a long-overdue lifeline for working families who have waited years for better service.

The mayor, who has championed the plan for two years, said the first new routes could open next spring, and dismissed the opposition as a radical fringe intent on blocking progress.

Opponents vowed to fight on, calling the vote a shameful betrayal of taxpayers and promising a lawsuit within weeks. The council's budget office expects the routes to carry about 12,000 riders a day.
